$comment: SeaBus operating assumptions. Geometry (berths, lanes) is in regions/metro-vancouver/infrastructure/seabus.json. OPEN-QUESTIONS #24.
$defaultPair: The berth every vessel uses at both terminals, unless AIS shows otherwise: when a day's docked fixes are mostly at the other pair's berths, that day is drawn along its paths (packages/transit-core/src/ais/match.ts). On a given day all vessels use west–west or east–east, with rare exceptions: the wheelhouse sees the passenger ramps better from one side, so a vessel always loads facing the same way (Braden, 2026-09-28). The timetable allows it: one vessel leaves at least 7 min before the next arrives, even at the weekday peak. Which pair is used varies by day and isn't known in advance; west is from the one sighting (Burrard Pacific Breeze at the West berths, 2026-09-26 14:15/14:29, Braden). guess
$ais: Live vessel positions from aisstream.io (docs/skytrain-viz-PLAN.md §4.12; key AISSTREAM_API_KEY in .secrets). The RT service's leader keeps one WebSocket open, records fixes to var/ais-history/ and serves them at /rt/ais/fixes; the browser turns them into timetable anchors (packages/transit-core/src/ais/match.ts).

ais.$vessels: MMSIs from MarineTraffic / VesselFinder / MyShipTracking, cross-checked (2026-09-28). Burrard Beaver is the spare.
ais.$boundingBox: Burrard Inlet around the crossing and the layup berth, [[lat, lon], [lat, lon]] (aisstream order).
ais.$batchS: Fixes are recorded in batches this often (an empty batch while connected keeps recorder coverage going).
ais.$coverageGapS: AIS recorder coverage breaks when consecutive batches are further apart than this (was shared with the bus recorder before its polling slowed; OPEN-QUESTIONS #29).
ais.$maxBackoffS: Reconnect backoff doubles from 5 s up to this.
ais.$match: Matching fixes to trips. 30-minute probe 2026-09-28 evening: per vessel in service, fixes a median ~60 s apart, gaps up to ~4 min; docked positions agree with the berth dock points to ~5 m. Guesses unless noted; OPEN-QUESTIONS #27.

match.$maxOffsetM: Lanes are traced to ±30 m and vessels wander ~100 m around them (AIS tracks).
match.$minTurnaroundS: Timetabled layovers are 2–4 min; a late vessel catches up by shortening them to this.
match.$pairMinFixes: The day's berth pair is the one with at least this many docked fixes, more than at every other pair together; until then, defaultPair.

ais.$glide: When new fixes arrive, vessels glide to their corrected position instead of jumping (packages/transit-core/src/ais/glide.ts, like buses): drawn behind, they catch up at up to catchUpMps extra over minGlideS–maxGlideS; drawn ahead, they hold (≤ maxHoldS). Under minM nothing changes; over snapM they jump. Guesses: the SeaBus cruises at ~6 m/s (AIS: 11–12.7 kn), so +4 m/s is a visible but plausible hurry.
